# Contract check: the immediate-return remember

**Date:** 2026-04-06
**Participants:** Wynn Castellano (Staff Engineer)

Wynn: "We ratified the async job contract: remember returns a receipt in
seconds and the extraction is watched by polling a cursor. No blocking
call, and no lost work if the client drops the receipt."

Key decision: remember dispatches, then the agent either polls the run or
gets the reaction piggybacked on a later call.

positions.name: RememberAsyncJobContract
positions.frame: How should the asynchronous job contract for remember structure dispatch, status retrieval, and result delivery to prevent blocking and loss of work?
positions.why: Both expressions define the mechanics of the async remember contract: Wynn confirms the ratified baseline of an immediate receipt, cursor polling, and resilience against dropped receipts, while Xena articulates the operational dispatch pattern enabling either active run polling or piggybacked reaction delivery on subsequent calls.

placements.why: Establishes the architectural stratum for asynchronous interaction contracts, dispatch lifecycles, and resilient status delivery mechanisms.
placements.title: standardizing asynchronous task execution, status polling, and reaction delivery
placements.frame: How do core service interfaces structure non-blocking job submission, receipt issuance, and execution tracking?

placements.title: from blocking synchronous calls to resilient asynchronous dispatch with cursor polling and piggybacked reactions
placements.frame: How should asynchronous extraction and dispatch contracts ensure work is preserved and non-blocking when receipts are dropped or results are retrieved across calls?
placements.why: Both Wynn and Xena define the ratified remember contract: returning immediate receipts, enabling cursor polling or piggybacked reactions, eliminating blocking calls, and preventing lost work if receipts drop.
